Telephone connections to senior citizens 
*361. SHRI ANIL SHARMA: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether senior citizens are provided telephone connections on priority 
basis; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) the number of applications recei ved by Government  from senior 
citizens for new telephone connections during January, 2002, in Gaya, Bihar, 
in general and Delha Mohalla in particular; and 
(d) by when these applications would be cleared and installation of 
telephones completed? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI PRAMOD MAHAJAN): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Senior 
citizens of the age of 65 years and above are entitled to register their demand 
for one telephone connection under No n-OYT Special category, which is 
given priority over general category. Fu rther, they are also exempted from 
payment of registration charges for registering their demand for new 
telephone connection. 
(c) The number of applications receive d during January, 2002 by Bharat 
Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) from senior citizens in Gaya Town of Bihar 
including Delha Mohalla is 28. Number of applications particularly from Delha 
Mohalla is 4. 
(d) These applicants are likely to be provided telephone connections by 
June, 2002.

Foodgrains Management Policy 
*363. SHRI P. PRABHAKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government's attention has been drawn to the news-report, 
captioned, "Foodgrains Management Policy in limbo" appearing in the Hindu 
dated the 8th March, 2002; 
(b) if so, by when a firm Foodgrains Management Policy is likely to be put 
in place; and 
(c) whether the opinion of the various State Governments with regard to the 
Foodgrains Management Policy is likely to be solicited before finalising the same 
and if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHANTA KUMAR): (a) Yes Sir. 
(b) The High Level Committee constituted by the Government of India under 
the Chairmanship of Prof. Abhijit Sen to formulate a Long Term Grain Policy is 
now expected to submit its report in May, 2002. The recommendations made by the 
said Committee will be duly examined and a new Grain Policy formulated 
expeditiously. 
(c) The High Level Committee has already held meetings with many State 
Governments. Further consultations with the State Governments will be held by 
the Government of India, if considered necessary, after the receipt of the report 
of the High Level Committee.

Over charging by PCOs 
†*364. SHRIMATI SAVITA S HARDA: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that PCOs in th e country are charging at old rates 
even now; 
(b) if so, whether Government are going to take any steps to check this; 
and 
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND 
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (SHRI PRAMOD 
MAHAJAN): (a) to (c) A few cases ha ve come to the notice where PCO 
booth operators were found using locally programmed charge indicators 
which is not permitted, which could have led to overcharging. Instructions 
have been issued to field units to carry out surprise checks of PCOs to ensure 
that PCO operators do not over charge the customers. Action, including 
disconnection, is taken against defaulters. 
Transit of foodgrains 
†*365. SHRI P.K. MAHESHWARI: W ill the Minister of CONSUMER 
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the agriculture experts have demanded Government for 
immediate repeal of the Essentia' Commodities Act, with a view to providing 
for unhindered transit of foodgrains in the country; 
(b) whether such demands had also been made previously; 
(c) if so, what are the reasons for not repealing the same; and 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
                                                     8 

[18 April, 2002]                 RAJYA SABHA 
(d) the action taken by Government on the demands raised by the experts? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHANTA KUMAR): (a) and (b) An expert 
Committee on Strengthening and Developing of Agricultural Marketing was set 
up by Government in the Ministry of Agriculture in December, 2000. The 
Committee in its report dated 29th June, 2001 recommended that the Essential 
Commodities Act, 19S5 under which restrictions have been imposed on storage and 
free movement of stocks, should be repealed to make way for play of free market 
forces in the real sense. 
(c) A standing Committee of some Union Ministers and Chief Ministers has 
been set up to look into issues relating to food management and agricultural 
exports. One of the issues identified was "Review of the Essential Commodities 
Act and Control Orders to ensure free movement of agricultural products". The 
Committee has suggested that the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 may continue 
as an umbrella legislation for the Centre and the States to use when needed, but a 
progressive dismantling of controls and restrictions was also required. 
(d) The Central Government have issued an Order under the Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955 allowing dealers to freely buy, stock, sell, transport, 
distribute, dispose, etc. any quantity in  respect of wheat, paddy/rice, coarse 
grains, sugar, edible oilseeds and edible oils without requiring any license or permit 
therefor under any order issued under the Act. The Order took effect after thirty 
days from the date of its issue (15.2.2002) notwithstanding anything to the 
contrary in any Order made by a State Government before the commencement of 
the Order.

*367. SHRI CO. POULOSE: 
             SHRI A. VIJAYA RAGHAVAN: 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether any study has been conducted on the viability of using rubber 
bitumen in constructing roads; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
10 

[18 April, 2002]                    RAJYA SABHA 
(c) whether Government of Kerala has sent any request to the Union 
Government seeking use of rubber bitumen in the construction of National 
Highways and other roads; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof along with the action taken by Government 
thereon? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT 
AND HIGHWAYS (MAJ. GEN. (RETD.) B.C. KHANDURI: (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) One study on the viability of using rubber/polymer modified bitumen 
was got conducted by the Ministry through Central Road Research Institute, 
New Delhi. This study has revealed that rubber/ polymer modified bitumen 
provides more durable roads by reducing susceptibility towards temperature 
variations and improving the desirable properties of bitumen thereby giving 
overall better performance. 
(c) and (d) The Government of Kerala have sent one proposal seeking 
use of rubberized bitumen in surfacing 12 km length of NH-213, which has 
been sanctioned. Besides, use of ruberized bitumen in surfacing has been 
approved for a length of about 24 km on NH-17 and NH-208 in Kerala, in 
surfacing under improvement of riding quality programme. 
Rise in buffer stock of foodgrains 
         *368.  SHRI RAJU PARMAR: 
                    SHRI BHAGATRAM MANHAR: 
Will the Minister of CONSUMER  AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the buffer stock of foodgrains by the end of this year 
is estimated to rise from the existing 580 lakh tonnes to more than 
675 lakh tonnes; 
(b) if so, what steps Government have taken or propose to take to tackle 
this problem; and 
(c) whether Government would consider to revamp the Public 
Distribution System (PDS) and if so, the details thereof? 
11 

RAJYA SABHA [18 April, 2002] 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHANTA KUMAR): (a) The total stocks of wheat 
and rice in the Central Pool as on 1.1.2002 were 580.32 lakh MTs. Keeping in 
view the likely procurement and off take during the year 2002, it was estimated 
that the total stocks of wheat and rice in the Central Pool as on 1.1.2003 would 
be 675.12 lakh MTs. 
(b) and (c) The Central Government  has recently taken the following 
measures to tackle this problem :— 
(i)  The allocation of foodgrains for Antyodaya and other BPL families 
under the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) has been 
increased from 25 kg. per family per month to 35 kg. per family per 
month. Further, the allocation for APL families has also been fixed at 
35 kg. per family per month with effect from 1.4.2002. 
(ii)    The Central Issue Prices (CIPs) for APL category have been reduced by 
Rs. 100 per quintal in respect of both rice and wheat with effect from 
1.4.2002. 
(iii)   The allocation for all welfare institutions and SC/ST/OBC hostels has 
been fixed uniformly at the rate of 15 kg. per head per month. An 
additional allocation equal to 5% of the BPL allocation of States/UTs 
has been made on this account at BPL rates. 
(iv)    50 lakh MTs of wheat and 10 lakh MTs of rice will be sold under the 
Open Market Sales Scheme during the year 2002-03. 
(v)  Quantitative restrictions on the export of rice, wheat and wheat 
products have been removed subject to the condition that the stocks in 
the Central Pool will not be lower than the buffer stock of 243 lakh MTs 
(100 lakh MTs of rice and 143 lakh MTs of wheat) at any point of time. 
Besides, to increase the export of wheat and rice, WTO compatible 
subsidies will be provided. 
12 

[18 April, 2002] RAJYA SABHA 
(vi) A decision has been taken to enter into counter trade and/or commodity 
assistance to other countries on te rms to be decided on case to case 
basis. 
As a result of the above measures, it is expected that the offtake of foodgrains 
from the Central Pool will increase by 160 lakh MTs in a full year. 
Lifting of control over foodgrains 
*369. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of 
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Governme nt have decided to free foodgrains 
from its control; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) by when Government arc going to introduce the Warehousing Receipt Act 
which would enable the farmers to go to a private owner of a warehouse for 
better price of their produce; and 
(d) what are the salient features of the proposed policy? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC 
DISTRIBUTION (SHRI SHANTA KUMAR): (a) and (b) The Central 
Government have issued an Order under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 
allowing dealers to freely buy, stock, sell, transport, distribute, dispose, etc. any 
quantity in respect of wheat, paddy/rice, coarse grains, sugar, edible oilseeds 
and edible oils without requiring any license or permit therefor under any order 
issued under the Act. The Order took effect after thirty days from the date of 
its issue (15.2.2002) notwithstanding anything to the country in any Order 
mad: by a State Government before the commencement of the Order. 
(c) and (d) An Expert Committee appointed by Government of India in the 
Ministry of Agriculture has inter-alia recommended to introduce a system of 
negotiable warehouse receipt in the country in respect of agricultural 
commodities for improved credit delivery,

Closing down of PCO/STD Booths in J&K 
*370. MIRZA ABDUL RASHID: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased 
to state: 
(a) the number of PCO and STD booths closed down in Jammu & Kashmir 
due to acute militancy, recently, district-wise; 
(b) how many employees have been rendered jobless and income-less in 
the State, district-wise; 
(c) what steps the Central and State Governments propose to take for 
rehabilitating such jobless youths in the State where lacs of educated youth 
have been facing unemployment; and 
(d) by when such PCO/STD booths would be revived? 
THE MINISTER OF COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI PRAMOD M AH A J AN): (a) to (c) No PCO booths 
was ordered to be closed. Only STD and ISD services were withdrawn on 
security considerations from all STD/ISD/PCOs in all districts in J&K except 
Leh and Kargil. Even though the STD/ISD facility has been withdrawn, the 
local call facility and 95 level dialling fa cility is available to all franchised 
PCOs and they can dial most of the places within the State. Consequently, 
while the franchisees may not have been rendered jobless and income less, 
their earnings would have been reduced. 
(d) Restoring STD/ISD in these PCOs can be considered only after the 
matter is reviewed by the concerned security agencies.

pleased to state: 
(a) whether Integrated Test Facilities (ITF) of Jessop and Company Ltd. is 
being treated as National Test House for testing of underground Mining Roof 
Supports for use in the Indian Mines; 
(b) if so, whether the same purpose can be served after the proposed
